note: Rules of thumb for weather go/no-go screening. Not engineering advice; project specs, the supplier, the engineer of record and manufacturer instructions win. Override any value by pointing RAINOUT_CONSTRUCTION_THRESHOLDS at a JSON file with the same shape (deep-merged).

sources.aci306: ACI PRC-306-16 (306R-16) Guide to Cold Weather Concreting: cold weather is when air temperature has fallen to, or is expected to fall below, 40 F (4 C) during the protection period; protect concrete from freezing until it reaches about 500 psi (3.5 MPa).
sources.aci305: ACI PRC-305-20 (305R-20) Guide to Hot Weather Concreting: hot weather precautions; plastic-shrinkage risk when the evaporation rate approaches 0.2 lb/ft2/h (1.0 kg/m2/h), lower (about 0.1 lb/ft2/h, 0.5 kg/m2/h) for low w/cm and silica-fume mixes. Evaporation estimate from the ACI 305 nomograph equation (Uno 1998).
sources.aci305_1: ACI SPEC-305.1-14: default maximum concrete temperature at delivery 95 F (35 C) unless specified otherwise; many project specs and suppliers use 90 F (32 C).
sources.ams_rain: AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'rain': light < 2.5 mm/h, moderate 2.5-7.6 mm/h, heavy > 7.6 mm/h.
sources.noaa_lightning: NOAA/NWS lightning safety ('When thunder roars, go indoors') and OSHA lightning fact sheet: stop outdoor work when thunderstorms are near.
sources.field_practice: Common field practice (PCA/NRMCA guidance such as NRMCA CIP 11 'Curing In-Place Concrete' and CIP 12 'Hot Weather Concreting'): do not place or finish in rain; fresh surfaces are vulnerable until final set, typically 2-4 h at about 70 F and longer in cool weather or with slag/fly ash or retarders. Exact rain amounts are rules of thumb, not code values.
sources.pump_wind: Concrete pump boom wind limits come from the manufacturer's manual (commonly around 35-40 mph); 35 mph gusts is a conservative screening value.
sources.gypsum_ga801: Gypsum Association GA-801, Handling and Storage of Gypsum Panel Products: store inside, off the ground, protected from weather; wet panels can lose strength and grow mold.
sources.apa_e30: APA Engineered Wood Construction Guide (Form E30): Exposure 1 panels tolerate normal construction delays, but prolonged wetting causes edge swelling; cover stacks and let panels dry before closing in.
sources.awc_lumber: American Wood Council / WWPA lumber storage guidance: store off the ground, covered and ventilated; framing should be at or below 19% moisture content before it is enclosed.
sources.pca_cement: Portland Cement Association: bagged cement hydrates with any moisture; store bags off the ground on pallets, tightly covered or indoors.
sources.nec_110_11: NFPA 70 (NEC) 110.11 Deteriorating Agents: equipment not identified for outdoor use must be protected against permanent damage from the weather during building construction.
sources.nwfa: National Wood Flooring Association installation guidelines: deliver and store flooring only in an enclosed, dry, climate-controlled building.
sources.bia_tn: Brick Industry Association Technical Notes (e.g. 7A, 23A): cover stockpiles and wall tops during construction to limit saturation and efflorescence.
sources.epa_swppp: EPA construction stormwater (SWPPP) guidance: stabilize open excavations and stockpiles before rain; inspect controls after 0.25 in or more.
sources.tarp_wind: Rule of thumb: loose tarps and poly start to lift around 25 mph gusts unless tied down and weighted.

drywall.label: drywall (gypsum board)
actions: Move it inside a dried-in space or onto pallets off the ground
Cover fully with tarps tied down on all sides
Replace any board that gets soaked

insulation.label: insulation (batts, rolls, loose fill)
actions: Keep it inside or in a closed trailer
Don't install until the building is dried in
Discard insulation that gets soaked

lumber.label: framing lumber
actions: Stack on stickers off the ground
Cover the top, leave the sides open to breathe
Let framing dry before closing in walls

osb.label: OSB or plywood sheathing
actions: Cover stacks and keep them off the ground
Install roof underlayment soon after the decking
Check for swollen edges before roofing or siding

cement_bags.label: bagged cement, mortar or grout
actions: Store on pallets under a roof or in a container
Wrap pallets in plastic and tie down
Don't use bags that have hardened lumps

open_roof_deck.label: open roof deck (no underlayment)
actions: Dry in with underlayment or roof tarps before the rain
Batten down tarp edges
Protect openings and interior finishes below

electrical.label: electrical equipment and rough-in
actions: Keep panels, devices and wire spools inside
Cap open boxes and conduit ends
Have equipment inspected if it got wet

flooring.label: wood or laminate flooring
actions: Deliver only into a dry, enclosed building
Leave it boxed and off slab or ground
Reschedule delivery if the building isn't dried in

masonry_units.label: brick or block
actions: Cover stockpiles and the tops of new walls

windows_doors.label: windows and doors not yet installed
actions: Store upright, inside or under cover
Keep factory wrap on

rebar.label: rebar and structural steel
actions: Light surface rust is normal; keep it off the ground and clear of mud

open_excavation.label: open excavation or trench
actions: Stabilize or cover spoil piles
Check silt fence and pumps
Inspect trench walls before re-entering after rain
